Zhou","__typename":"User"},"body":"#### Overview ####\r\nA new `\u003camp-consent\u003e` component that enables publisher to get consents from readers and manage their consents. \r\n\r\n#### Format ####\r\n```\r\n\u003camp-consent\u003e\r\n   \u003cscript type='application/json'\u003e{\r\n     “consents”: {\r\n        “consentInstanceABC”: {\r\n           “checkConsentHref”: “endpointABC.com”,\r\n           “promptUI”: “template1”\r\n         },\r\n        “consentInstanceDEF”: {\r\n           “checkConsentHref”: “endpointDEF.com”,\r\n           “promptUI”: “template2”\r\n         }\r\n      },\r\n     “policy”: {\r\n         “policyABC”: {\r\n             “waitFor”: {\r\n                “consentInstanceABC”: [],\r\n              }\r\n           }\r\n     }\r\n   }\u003c/script\u003e\r\n   \u003cdiv id=”template1”\u003e\r\n     Collect consent for instance ABC\r\n     \u003cbutton on=\"tap:consentInstanceABC.dismiss\"\u003eDismiss\u003c/button\u003e\r\n     \u003cbutton on=\"tap:consentInstanceABC.accept\"\u003eAccept\u003c/button\u003e\r\n     \u003cbutton on=\"tap:consentInstanceABC.decline\"\u003eDecline\u003c/button\u003e\r\n   \u003c/div\u003e\r\n   \u003cdiv id=”template2”\u003e\r\n     Can we use your cookie?\r\n     \u003cbutton on=\"tap:consentInstanceDEF.accept\"\u003eAccept\u003c/button\u003e\r\n   \u003c/div\u003e\r\n \u003c/amp-consent\u003e\r\n```\r\n\r\n#### Consent instance ####\r\n\r\n##### config #####\r\nEach unique consent instance keeps a list of endpoints to get and update consent states. Initially, the configuration is simple:\r\n* checkConsentHref: An endpoint to use to check the consent status\r\n* promptUI: An ID corresponding to the UI container to display that's meant to collect this consent.\r\n\r\nIn the future, configuration options may be expanded for more functionality:\r\n\r\n```\r\n{\r\n  checkConsentHref: (required)\r\n  promptUI: (required)\r\n  disableLocalStorage: (optional) true/false. Default to false - controls whether state does not get kept in local storage (see below)\r\n  acceptHref: (optional) - an endpoint that is requested when the consent is accepted\r\n  rejectHref: (optional) - an endpoint that is requested when the consent is rejected\r\n  dismissHref: (optional) -  - an endpoint that is requested when the consent is dimissed\r\n}\r\n```\r\n##### checkConsentHref #####\r\nRequest\r\n\r\nMake a `POST` request:\r\n```\r\n{\r\n  consentInstanceId // string for the consent ID being asked about\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nIn the future, this may be expanded to include:\r\n```\r\n{\r\n  consentInstanceId // string for the consent ID being asked about\r\n  ampUserId // For server to identify the user\r\n  timestamp // value stored on client side, can be empty\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nResponse\r\n\r\nExpect a response with an boolean value:\r\n```\r\n{\r\n  'promptIfUnknown': boolean (true/false)\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n#### Consent Policy ####\r\n\r\nA default consent policy will be auto generated to wait for every consent instance. One can overwrite the default consent policy by declaring a new consent policy instance with id `\"default\"`. Or add other consent policy instances to the `\u003camp-consent\u003e` config.\r\n\r\n##### Consent Policy Instance Config #####\r\nEach unique consent policy instance creates a consent blocking behavior unit that instruct other components on the page. It keeps a list of consent instances to wait for. \u003camp-consent> component ","articleBody":"#### Overview ####\r\nA new `\u003camp-consent>` component that enables publisher to get consents from readers and manage their consents. \r\n\r\n#### Format ####\r\n```\r\n\u003camp-consent>\r\n   \u003cscript type='application/json'>{\r\n     “consents”: {\r\n        “consentInstanceABC”: {\r\n           “checkConsentHref”: “endpointABC.com”,\r\n           “promptUI”: “template1”\r\n         },\r\n        “consentInstanceDEF”: {\r\n           “checkConsentHref”: “endpointDEF.com”,\r\n           “promptUI”: “template2”\r\n         }\r\n      },\r\n     “policy”: {\r\n         “policyABC”: {\r\n             “waitFor”: {\r\n                “consentInstanceABC”: [],\r\n              }\r\n           }\r\n     }\r\n   }\u003c/script>\r\n   \u003cdiv id=”template1”>\r\n     Collect consent for instance ABC\r\n     \u003cbutton on=\"tap:consentInstanceABC.dismiss\">Dismiss\u003c/button>\r\n     \u003cbutton on=\"tap:consentInstanceABC.accept\">Accept\u003c/button>\r\n     \u003cbutton on=\"tap:consentInstanceABC.decline\">Decline\u003c/button>\r\n   \u003c/div>\r\n   \u003cdiv id=”template2”>\r\n     Can we use your cookie?\r\n     \u003cbutton on=\"tap:consentInstanceDEF.accept\">Accept\u003c/button>\r\n   \u003c/div>\r\n \u003c/amp-consent>\r\n```\r\n\r\n#### Consent instance ####\r\n\r\n##### config #####\r\nEach unique consent instance keeps a list of endpoints to get and update consent states. Initially, the configuration is simple:\r\n* checkConsentHref: An endpoint to use to check the consent status\r\n* promptUI: An ID corresponding to the UI container to display that's meant to collect this consent.\r\n\r\nIn the future, configuration options may be expanded for more functionality:\r\n\r\n```\r\n{\r\n  checkConsentHref: (required)\r\n  promptUI: (required)\r\n  disableLocalStorage: (optional) true/false. Default to false - controls whether state does not get kept in local storage (see below)\r\n  acceptHref: (optional) - an endpoint that is requested when the consent is accepted\r\n  rejectHref: (optional) - an endpoint that is requested when the consent is rejected\r\n  dismissHref: (optional) -  - an endpoint that is requested when the consent is dimissed\r\n}\r\n```\r\n##### checkConsentHref #####\r\nRequest\r\n\r\nMake a `POST` request:\r\n```\r\n{\r\n  consentInstanceId // string for the consent ID being asked about\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nIn the future, this may be expanded to include:\r\n```\r\n{\r\n  consentInstanceId // string for the consent ID being asked about\r\n  ampUserId // For server to identify the user\r\n  timestamp // value stored on client side, can be empty\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nResponse\r\n\r\nExpect a response with an boolean value:\r\n```\r\n{\r\n  'promptIfUnknown': boolean (true/false)\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n#### Consent Policy ####\r\n\r\nA default consent policy will be auto generated to wait for every consent instance. One can overwrite the default consent policy by declaring a new consent policy instance with id `\"default\"`. Or add other consent policy instances to the `\u003camp-consent>` config.\r\n\r\n##### Consent Policy Instance Config #####\r\nEach unique consent policy instance creates a consent blocking behavior unit that instruct other components on the page. It keeps a list of consent instances to wait for. Initially, the configuration is simple:\r\n* waitFor: A JSON object that declare the list of consents to wait. \r\n```\r\n'waitFor': {\r\n  'ABC': [] // Only empty array accept now.  \r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nIn the future, configuration options may be expanded for more functionality:\r\n```\r\n{\r\n  'waitFor': {\r\n    'consentId': [] // Array of items that's associated with that consent instance\r\n  }\r\n  'timeout': timeout in case user never respond\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n#### Storage ####\r\n\r\nAll consent instance state will be stored and handled client side. \r\nFor each consent instance. LocalStorage looks like\r\n* Key: `amp-consent:${consentInstanceId}`\r\n* Value: true/false (won’t store anything for unknown state)\r\n\r\n#### Blocking Components ####\r\nUse `data-block-on-consent=consent-policy-id` to block AMP components with consents. If no `consent-policy-id` is specified, `\"default\"` consent policy instance will be used. \r\n\r\nIndividual AMP component can override default blocking behaviors and implement blocking logic itself. \r\n\r\n#### UI ####\r\n\r\nUI Restrictions\r\n\r\nPrompt UI\r\n  * Only a single \u003camp-consent> UI can be shown at a time.\r\n  * Position fixed and stick to the bottom of the page\r\n\r\nRevocation button\r\n  * Will only be displayed after consent state is determined\r\n  * Can overlap when there are multiple consent instances. \r\n\r\nText\r\n  * All text will be static inlined. No template replacing will be supported\r\n\r\n\r\n##### Revocation Button Design #####\r\nComing soon, we will support the ability to specify a UI container that will be displayed once the prompt has been handled. This can be used optionally to enable a persistent UI affordance to be displayed that allows the end user to revoke their previous choice and pick a new class="markdown-body" data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><h4 dir="auto">Overview</h4>
<p dir="auto">A new <code class="notranslate"><amp-consent></code> component that enables publisher to get consents from readers and manage their consents.</p>
<h4 dir="auto">Format</h4>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="<amp-consent>
   <script type='application/json'>{
     “consents”: {
        “consentInstanceABC”: {
           “checkConsentHref”: “endpointABC.com”,
           “promptUI”: “template1”
         },
        “consentInstanceDEF”: {
           “checkConsentHref”: “endpointDEF.com”,
           “promptUI”: “template2”
         }
      },
     “policy”: {
         “policyABC”: {
             “waitFor”: {
                “consentInstanceABC”: [],
              }
           }
     }
   }</script>
   <div id=”template1”>
     Collect consent for instance ABC
     <button on="tap:consentInstanceABC.dismiss">Dismiss</button>
     <button on="tap:consentInstanceABC.accept">Accept</button>
     <button on="tap:consentInstanceABC.decline">Decline</button>
   </div>
   <div id=”template2”>
     Can we use your cookie?
     <button on="tap:consentInstanceDEF.accept">Accept</button>
   </div>
 </amp-consent>"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate"><amp-consent>
   <script type='application/json'>{
     “consents”: {
        “consentInstanceABC”: {
           “checkConsentHref”: “endpointABC.com”,
           “promptUI”: “template1”
         },
        “consentInstanceDEF”: {
           “checkConsentHref”: “endpointDEF.com”,
           “promptUI”: “template2”
         }
      },
     “policy”: {
         “policyABC”: {
             “waitFor”: {
                “consentInstanceABC”: [],
              }
           }
     }
   }</script>
   <div id=”template1”>
     Collect consent for instance ABC
     <button on="tap:consentInstanceABC.dismiss">Dismiss</button>
     <button on="tap:consentInstanceABC.accept">Accept</button>
     <button on="tap:consentInstanceABC.decline">Decline</button>
   </div>
   <div id=”template2”>
     Can we use your cookie?
     <button on="tap:consentInstanceDEF.accept">Accept</button>
   </div>
 </amp-consent>
</code></pre></div>
<h4 dir="auto">Consent instance</h4>
<h5 dir="auto">config</h5>
<p dir="auto">Each unique consent instance keeps a list of endpoints to get and update consent states. Initially, the configuration is simple:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>checkConsentHref: An endpoint to use to check the consent status</li>
<li>promptUI: An ID corresponding to the UI container to display that's meant to collect this consent.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">In the future, configuration options may be expanded for more functionality:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="{
  checkConsentHref: (required)
  promptUI: (required)
  disableLocalStorage: (optional) true/false. Default to false - controls whether state does not get kept in local storage (see below)
  acceptHref: (optional) - an endpoint that is requested when the consent is accepted
  rejectHref: (optional) - an endpoint that is requested when the consent is rejected
  dismissHref: (optional) -  - an endpoint that is requested when the consent is dimissed
}"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">{
  checkConsentHref: (required)
  promptUI: (required)
  disableLocalStorage: (optional) true/false. Default to false - controls whether state does not get kept in local storage (see below)
  acceptHref: (optional) - an endpoint that is requested when the consent is accepted
  rejectHref: (optional) - an endpoint that is requested when the consent is rejected
  dismissHref: (optional) -  - an endpoint that is requested when the consent is dimissed
}
</code></pre></div>
<h5 dir="auto">checkConsentHref</h5>
<p dir="auto">Request</p>
<p dir="auto">Make a <code class="notranslate">POST</code> request:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="{
  consentInstanceId // string for the consent ID being asked about
}"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">{
  consentInstanceId // string for the consent ID being asked about
}
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">In the future, this may be expanded to include:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="{
  consentInstanceId // string for the consent ID being asked about
  ampUserId // For server to identify the user
  timestamp // value stored on client side, can be empty
}"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">{
  consentInstanceId // string for the consent ID being asked about
  ampUserId // For server to identify the user
  timestamp // value stored on client side, can be empty
}
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Response</p>
<p dir="auto">Expect a response with an boolean value:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="{
  'promptIfUnknown': boolean (true/false)
}"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">{
  'promptIfUnknown': boolean (true/false)
}
</code></pre></div>
<h4 dir="auto">Consent Policy</h4>
<p dir="auto">A default consent policy will be auto generated to wait for every consent instance. One can overwrite the default consent policy by declaring a new consent policy instance with id <code class="notranslate">"default"</code>. Or add other consent policy instances to the <code class="notranslate"><amp-consent></code> config.</p>
<h5 dir="auto">Consent Policy Instance Config</h5>
<p dir="auto">Each unique consent policy instance creates a consent blocking behavior unit that instruct other components on the page. It keeps a list of consent instances to wait for. Initially, the configuration is simple:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>waitFor: A JSON object that declare the list of consents to wait.</li>
</ul>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="'waitFor': {
  'ABC': [] // Only empty array accept now.  
}"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">'waitFor': {
  'ABC': [] // Only empty array accept now.  
}
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">In the future, configuration options may be expanded for more functionality:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="{
  'waitFor': {
    'consentId': [] // Array of items that's associated with that consent instance
  }
  'timeout': timeout in case user never respond
}"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">{
  'waitFor': {
    'consentId': [] // Array of items that's associated with that consent instance
  }
  'timeout': timeout in case user never respond
}
</code></pre></div>
<h4 dir="auto">Storage</h4>
<p dir="auto">All consent instance state will be stored and handled client side.<br>
For each consent instance. LocalStorage looks like</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Key: <code class="notranslate">amp-consent:${consentInstanceId}</code></li>
<li>Value: true/false (won’t store anything for unknown state)</li>
</ul>
<h4 dir="auto">Blocking Components</h4>
<p dir="auto">Use <code class="notranslate">data-block-on-consent=consent-policy-id</code> to block AMP components with consents. If no <code class="notranslate">consent-policy-id</code> is specified, <code class="notranslate">"default"</code> consent policy instance will be used.</p>
<p dir="auto">Individual AMP component can override default blocking behaviors and implement blocking logic itself.</p>
<h4 dir="auto">UI</h4>
<p dir="auto">UI Restrictions</p>
<p dir="auto">Prompt UI</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Only a single  UI can be shown at a time.</li>
<li>Position fixed and stick to the bottom of the page</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Revocation button</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Will only be displayed after consent state is determined</li>
<li>Can overlap when there are multiple consent instances.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Text</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>All text will be static inlined. No template replacing will be supported</li>
</ul>
<h5 dir="auto">Revocation Button Design</h5>
<p dir="auto">Coming soon, we will support the ability to specify a UI container that will be displayed once the prompt has been handled. This can be used optionally to enable a persistent UI affordance to be displayed that allows the end user to revoke their previous choice and pick a new choice.</p></div></div><div data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">@ayumihamsaki there are a number of subtle differences which are designed to comply with the detail in the GDPR. Amongst other things;</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>consent:</strong> the user should be given ability to optin or out, a solo accept button is equivalent to a pre-ticked box (which is non-compliant),</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>storage:</strong> You are required to keep an up-to-date record of users preference status and be able to demonstrate that record upon request (local storage in this instance), and</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>optout:</strong> The user should be able to change their mind with as much ease as they opted in, preferably using the same mechanism (DP by design).</p>
<p dir="auto">There is a bunch more reasons. It's worth noting that cookies are one of the most ambiguous topics of the GDPR, mentioned one (I recall) but included in the scope without much direction on how to comply. It is the EU's view that much of the data collected using cookies can be used alone or in combination to pinpoint a specific users (IP, GA snippet, Zip or postcode) so it is well within scope.</p>

data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">We wanted to update this thread with some features we plan to implement in the future. Please note that we haven't committed to implement all the features and the final set will be based on the feedback we receive after amp-consent has been launched.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>'checkConsentHref' related</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Enhance ‘checkConsentHref’ to respond with additional key value pairs, including support for variable substitution that can be sent to components that are blocked on consent</li>
<li>Use <a href="https://github.com/ampproject/amphtml/issues/14280" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/ampproject/amphtml/issues/14280/hovercard">amp-geo</a> to selectively trigger consent if the user is from a certain country</li>
<li>Use <a href="https://github.com/ampproject/amphtml/issues/14280" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/ampproject/amphtml/issues/14280/hovercard">amp-geo</a> to configure different consent UIs for users from different countries</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Others</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Get consent markup in real-time instead of hardcoding it in the document</li>
<li>Support making consent buttons active only upon reading the entire consent by the user (e.g. needing to scroll all the way to the bottom indicating that the user has read the content)</li>
<li>Support for multiple amp-consents to work sequentially</li>
<li>Get amp-consent to work sequentially with amp-user-notification</li>
<li>[updated after comment below]Support per vendor consent. i.e. User should be able to accept consent on a per vendor basis.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Please add any other features that we've missed to consider or upvote any of the features with a comment.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 in reality its hard to know.</p>
<p dir="auto">However, it is important that not consenting is not the same as avoiding advertising.  Looking at some of the examples and ideas shown in  seems to show that this can be used to show / not show parts of the page.</p>
<p dir="auto">In the case of advertising that consent / non consent needs to be passed into the advertising system so that the advertising network (tool) can decide what to serve the user even if they can't use cookies.</p>
<p dir="auto">Page 16/17 of <a href="http://advertisingconsent.eu/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/Transparency-Consent-Framework-Presentation-Website.pdf" rel="nofollow">http://advertisingconsent.eu/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/Transparency-Consent-Framework-Presentation-Website.pdf</a> give some examples of what a pop up might look like and in the case of mobile devices this is a more complex version of the current (accept cookies banner that many have).</p>
<p dir="auto">The key is can the amp-consent tool be sophisticated enough to ask the intial question and if a person wants granularity punt them to a part of the site to complete the process.</p>
<p dir="auto">I don't know the answer but with a month until GDPR goes live there are many more questions than answers for these questions.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" <p dir="auto">For example for amp-ad components I don't want to block these from rendering outright, but would prefer the ad to receive the users consent status, so that we can serve a house ad to users who opt-out.</p>

<p dir="auto">That exact use case is supported! amp-consent itself don't block the ad request, it just makes the state available to the ad network to do whatever is appropriate. For e.g. when a user rejects consent, the state <a href="https://github.com/ampproject/amphtml/blob/master/extensions/amp-consent/customizing-extension-behaviors-on-consent.md#advanced-blocking-behaviors">CONSENT_POLICY_STATE.INSUFFICIENT</a> is made available to the ad network and they could choose non-personalized ads at that point.<br>
For e.g. I know DoubleClick is in process of consuming the flag in this way.</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Individual components may override this behavior to provide more specialized handling. Please refer to each component's documentation for details.</p>

<p dir="auto"><a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/clumsyjedi/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/clumsyjedi">@clumsyjedi</a> That's a good point for amp-iframe. For amp-ad, we will ask each ad vendor to specify whether they will handle consent state themselves. But for amp-iframe, it will require the publisher to instruct AMP whether the iframe will handle consent blocking or not. We can expose an attribute for that.</p>
</blockquote>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/clumsyjedi/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/clumsyjedi">@clumsyjedi</a> <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/zhouyx/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/zhouyx">@zhouyx</a> for amp-iframe the default could be to block if data-block-on-consent is present. Only allowing it to run, passing in the consent state, if consent has resolved and data-consent-aware-iframe (of something similar) is set.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/jpettitt/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/jpettitt">@jpettitt</a> <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/zhouyx/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/zhouyx">@zhouyx</a> My use case is that we have call backs to our own site for rich content in iframes. We want to render the iframe content regardless of consent state.</p>
<p dir="auto">For the consent states UNKNOWN, REJECTED and DISMISSED we would render the content without any tracking.</p>
<p dir="auto">For the states NOT_REQUIRED and GRANTED we would render the content with tracking scripts in it.</p>
<p dir="auto">So to me it's important that the iframe have access to the consent state to make that determination. Our iframes are embedded using the <code class="notranslate">src</code> attribute of AMP iframe. I would like to see something like a <code class="notranslate">consent-status-parameter</code> attribute on the amp-iframe element, which would contain REJECTED|GRANTED|etc. So <code class="notranslate">consent-status-parameter=gamp-consent-status</code> would append <code class="notranslate">gamp-consent-status=GRANTED</code> to the query string in the <code class="notranslate">src</code> parameter.</p>
<p dir="auto">I assume other publishers who embed using <code class="notranslate">srcdoc</code> would also need the consent state communicated to the iframe document. I don't know what mechanism could be used... can a CONSENT_STATUS var be injected into the iframed document?</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1
